description: The Zenodo deposit authors curated 560 laboratory soil-strength observations from 20 peer-reviewed studies of biopolymer and multi-additive stabilisation. It separates 397 unconfined compressive strength results from 163 California Bearing Ratio results. Each row identifies an experimental condition such as soil and stabiliser type, compaction, curing time and test conditions. The public XLSX workbook includes cleaned tables, source-study inventory, data dictionary, vocabulary map and quality-control log. The repository lists CC BY 4.0 and no price. For simulation, transport modellers could use these tests to bound pavement-subgrade strength assumptions or compare stabilisation choices in road resilience and maintenance planning. These are laboratory conditions, not geocoded road assets or proven field performance; some values were digitised from figures, and the source studies differ. The workbook was not downloaded, so its numerical entries and quality flags remain untested. This record is related to the catalogue New Zealand Geotechnical Database as material-property evidence, but that database contains site investigation records. The earlier built-environment screen did not assess road use.
